parent_models.justification: A goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy is essentially a special type of conditional policy where the condition is the goal. Therefore, 'conditional policy' acts as a broad category that includes goal-conditioned policies.
Similar to a goal-conditioned policy, a context-conditioned policy can include many forms of conditioning, such as goals, making it a parent model to more specific conditioned policies.

closest_parent_model.justification: Out of the parent models, 'conditional policy' is more directly aligned with goal-conditioning as it specifically refers to policies conditioned on various factors, whereas 'context' can be broader than just goals.

child_models.justification: This model likely refers to a more specific technique within goal-conditioned settings, implying a specific approach to handling goals, making it a child model.

closest_child_model.justification: Since 'latent diffusion goal conditioning' specifically mentions goal conditioning, it is the closest child model to a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning policy.

sibling_models.justification: Both are specific strategies within the broader context of reinforcement learning. While one focuses on goal-condition reinforcement learning, the other focuses on imitation learning within reinforcement learning.
